manifesto: The primary virtue of a cleaning tool is not simply freeing disk space, but ensuring no developer source code or personal data is ever damaged. Detergo adheres strictly to these rules:
All operations dispatch items via the native Windows Shell COM API to the Recycle Bin. Users can restore any folder in one click at any time.
Symlinks and NTFS Junction points are strictly excluded during scan and deletion. Any reparse point pointing outside the project tree (such as C:\\Windows or ~/.ssh) is immediately blocked.
If an active Node.js, Cargo, or IDE process holds a lock on a target folder, Detergo never forces deletion; it safely skips the target and reports it in the summary.

safety-architecture: Defensive architectures applied by Detergo against Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race conditions:
Right before deletion, the directory handle is inspected via
. If the target was transformed into a Junction or Symlink, deletion is instantly aborted.
For targets temporarily locked by antivirus or indexers, operations retry at 100ms, 250ms, and 500ms intervals before skipping gracefully.
system-cleaner: Reclaim space on the system drive without typing a single command. Every action is measured before anything is deleted.

The cleaner covers your temporary files, Windows temporary files, Prefetch data, Windows Update leftovers, Windows error reports, the Recycle Bin, the Windows Disk Cleanup profile and the component store (WinSxS). Project folders, documents and Downloads sit outside every audited root and can never be selected.

Windows blocks system folders for standard users. When an action needs elevation the page offers a single restart button; the app reopens on the same page with your selection intact. The app itself still starts without administrator rights, so scanning and cleaning your own files never needs a prompt.

The interface only sends action identifiers; paths are resolved and re-verified on the native side against a fixed audited list. Deletion never follows junctions or symbolic links, locked files are skipped and reported, and every run is written to the local audit history.
Nothing is uploaded. Sizes, logs and audit records stay on this device.

A Windows scheduled task can run the quick or standard profile daily or weekly. The task runs with the highest rights your account allows and asks nothing; remove the schedule from the same panel at any time. Prefetch, the Recycle Bin and the component store are never chosen automatically.

webhook-schema: Standard JSON payload dispatched to the webhook target upon completion:

Field reference event is always scan or clean . The legacy names scan_completed and cleanup_completed are accepted as aliases and are rewritten to the canonical names before delivery. timestamp , product and version identify the installation that raised the event; the payload is never signed. status is success , partial (the scan stopped early) or cancelled (the user pressed Stop). total_bytes is the reclaimable space that was measured; total_human is its formatted form. cleaned_count and cleaned_bytes only appear on cleanup events. Scan events also carry scan_id , root_path , duration_ms and, when the result is partial, stop_reason . Cleanup events from the desktop app also carry plan_id , mode , success_count , error_count , moved_bytes and reclaim_bytes . )}
